verdict.rationale: Supermemory's docs say it automatically extracts memories from raw content, including conversations, and builds user profiles that it maintains automatically from all interactions and updates as users interact. Its living knowledge graph of facts and incremental processing via customId suggest ongoing consolidation, but background or asynchronous consolidation is never stated outright. missing for 10: explicit documentation that consolidation (merging, deduplication, superseding facts) runs in the background, detail on how salience is judged when deciding what is worth remembering, and independent or hands-on corroboration of extraction quality.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the memory layer decides for itself what is worth remembering — extracting salient facts from raw conversation and consolidating them in the background

citations.quote: Send any raw content to Supermemory — conversations, documents, files, URLs. We extract the memories automatically.
User profiles are **automatically maintained collections of facts about your users** that Supermemory builds from all their interactions.
Profiles update as users interact with your system
Supermemory builds a living knowledge graph of facts on top of other facts — not a static folder of embeddings
When you send content with the same customId, Supermemory intelligently processes only what's new.
